messages.subject: observed data files
parts:
Hi,
I have a few questions on the observed data files as I could not figure this out from the examples:
1. Should he maximum number of decimal places for the Qobs == 2? Or is this just a feature of your example data.
2. Are the column titles fixed, or can then be different?
3. Missing data can be indicated in the Flag column and you can use NA as well, but what is not clear is if the dates need to be continuous, or can the dates be discontinuous (i.e. missing data removed from the observed file)?

Thanks
Willem

messages.author: e28329d3e25e358e
messages.subject: Re: observed data files
parts:
Hi Willem,

Thank you for your interest in this tool. This topic, format of the observed data file, hasn't been mentioned in such a detail before

1. Should the maximum number of decimal places for the Qobs == 2? Or is this just a feature of your example data.
ANSWER: It can be any number of decimal places, for e.g.,  6.963123 and 6.963 and 6.96e0 are all valid numbers
2. Are the column titles fixed, or can then be different?

ANSWER: The column title will NOT be read by R-SWAT, it is just for user to know that the first column should be date, 2nd column is time, 3rd column is data, and 4th column is Flag. Therefore, user can use different names as suggested by the observed template file. For example, the following titles are both valid

Column title 1: "Date  time   Qobs  Flag"
Column title 2 "myDate Time  Qoutlet Flag  This is the title line and will not be read"

3. Missing data can be indicated in the Flag column and you can use NA as well, but what is not clear is if the dates need to be continuous, or can the dates be discontinuous (i.e. missing data removed from the observed file)?

ANSWER: You are right, missing values can be 1) in the data column (3rd column) or in the Flag column (4th column) or 2) in both data and Flag column

The date MUST BE continuous if you calibrate your model at daily time step
The month also MUST BE continuous if you calibrate your model at monthly time step
The year also MUST BE continuous if you calibrate your model at yearly time step

Therefore, if there is a date (or month or year) that no measurement, just put that date into the observed file with missing values (in the 3rd and/or 4th column)

If you used the option "UserReadSwatOutput" (in Step 3. Run SWAT => Tab 1. Define model outputs for extraction) then the observed data file of THIS output variable could be discontinuous - depending on whether you read the entire output data our just the data of some specific date in your code

4. Attached is the figure and example of obs_var_1.txt with various number formats that are all valid in R-SWAT
5. And I have further questions. Am I correct that for your example SWAT project the outlet is subbasin 20?
ANSWER: In my example SWAT project I have only 7 basins and the outlet is in subbasins. This file was removed from the latest R-SWAT update but can be found in version 1.0.0, which is available from the link below, just extract this file, it is in the folder data\Watershed\Shapes\subs1.shp

https://github.com/tamnva/R-SWAT/archive/refs/tags/v1.0.0.zip

I think you question is about example SWAT+ data, I did not prepared this data. You could get more information about example SWAT+ data from here
https://chrisschuerz.github.io/SWATplusR/articles/SWATplusR.html

6. And what version of the executable should be used for the examples? The latest? or the older version 670 that works with the free SWAT_CUP
ANSWER: I have tried with different (including  the latest) versions of SWAT/SWAT+. It should works with different executable SWAT versions

Cheers,
Tam

messages.subject: Re: observed data files
parts: Hi, there is no difference. R-SWAT will ignore that observed value (for calibration or validation) if you put 1) NA in the value column, OR (2) NA in the Cali_Valid_Flag column, OR (3) NA in both observed and Cali_Valid_Flag column
